verdict.rationale: Phaser's docs say games can target the web or be compiled to iOS, Android, Steam and native desktop apps, but only through unnamed third-party tools rather than a built-in exporter. Community reports confirm wrapping Phaser games as Android/iOS apps (Cocoon, an APK at 60fps), though one user hit slow WebGL in iOS webviews under Cordova. Console export is never mentioned, directly or via partners. Missing for 10: any console export path (direct or partner), a first-party desktop/mobile export pipeline instead of unnamed 3rd-party tools, documented build workflows for each target.

support.subject: As a studio lead, one project exports to desktop, mobile, and (directly or via partners) consoles

citations.quote: Games can be built for the web, or as YouTube Playables, Discord Activies, Twitch Overlays or compiled to iOS, Android, Steam and native apps using 3rd party tools.
There are ways to convert browser games to native mobile or desktop apps using 3rd party tools, and many Phaser developers have done this successfully.
used cocoon to package it up into an Android and iOS app
exported it to an android .apk and easily runs at 60fps on Nexus 7.
